facts.value: Moderate exercise has a beneficial effect on the human immune system.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Moderate exercise has been associated with a 29% decreased incidence of upper respiratory tract infections (URTI).
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Prolonged high-intensity exercise, such as marathon training, is associated with an increased risk of infection occurrence.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Immune cell functions are impaired following acute sessions of prolonged, high-intensity exercise.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Strenuous stress for long durations can suppress the immune system by decreasing the concentration of lymphocytes.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: The immune systems of athletes and nonathletes are generally similar.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Athletes may have a slightly elevated natural killer cell count and cytolytic action.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Vitamin C supplementation has been associated with a lower incidence of upper respiratory tract infections in marathon runners.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Biomarkers of inflammation such as C-reactive protein are reduced in active individuals relative to sedentary individuals.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: In individuals with heart disease, exercise interventions lower blood levels of fibrinogen and C-reactive protein.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: The depression in the immune system following acute bouts of exercise may be one of the mechanisms for the anti-inflammatory effect.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc
